observation_summary: The Week constructor was incorrectly using a default time zone constant instead of the provided time zone parameter when initializing the object, leading to incorrect week calculations.
hypothesis: The constructor `Week(Date time, TimeZone zone)` was incorrectly passing `RegularTimePeriod.DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE` to the chained constructor instead of the `zone` argument provided by the caller.
prediction: The fix will change the argument passed to the chained constructor from `RegularTimePeriod.DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE` to `zone`.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows exactly this change: `this(time, RegularTimePeriod.DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE, Locale.getDefault());` was changed to `this(time, zone, Locale.getDefault());`.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of using the wrong variable (a hardcoded default constant) instead of the provided parameter during object initialization. This is a direct assignment/initialization error. It is not an Algorithm/Method error because the logic of the constructor itself is fine; it just received the wrong input due to the incorrect assignment. It is not a Checking error because no validation was missing.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the change from `RegularTimePeriod.DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE` to `zone` in the `Week` constructor.
The failing test `testConstructor` expected 35 but got 34, indicating the time zone used for calculation was incorrect.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The procedure itself is correct; the error is simply that the wrong value (the default constant) was passed to the constructor.
The interface signature was correct; the implementation of the constructor simply failed to use the provided parameter correctly.
